chunks: Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ narrated from Ṣafwān, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If the man who has performed ẓihār fasts one month and fasts one day from the other month, then he has maintained consecutiveness. Then if he wishes, let him complete the remainder separately, and if he wishes, let him give for each day one mudd of food.

key_terms.الشَّهْرِ: the month, referring here to the required fasting period
key_terms.الْمُظَاهِرُ: the man who has pronounced ẓihār against his wife
key_terms.فَلْيَقْضِ: let him complete or make up what remains
key_terms.مُدًّا: a mudd, a fixed measure of food
key_terms.وَاصَلَ: he has maintained the required continuity

ai.seo_question: When is consecutive fasting considered fulfilled in the kaffarah of ẓihār?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the kaffarah of ẓihār and the requirement of consecutive fasting. It states that after completing one full month and one day of the second month, the condition of continuity is achieved, after which the remaining days may be completed non-consecutively or compensated by feeding for each day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4841 - Ayyub ibn Nuh narrated from Safwan, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"If a man who has performed ẓihar fasts for one full month and then fasts a day from the second month, he has fulfilled the condition of consecutive fasting. After that, if he wishes, he may make up the remaining fasts in a non-consecutive manner, or if he wishes, he may give a mudd (a specific measure) of food for each remaining day."
